prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S152: The Control Room Operator uses the acknowledgement slip to record the alarm response and any outstanding action.
S153: The operator checks available device status and sequence information without treating a cleared indication as proof that the underlying cause has been corrected.
S154: The Feeder Protection Relay indication is reviewed against the affected feeder status and any related protection operation.
S155: The Bay Automation Controller provides bay-level status indications that support the operator’s assessment of the alarm.
S156: Glasswing shall retain alarm state and event information for operator review after an indication has cleared.
S157: The Sequence Event Archive provides time-ordered evidence for later operational review.
S158: The North Protection Panel contains the protection equipment associated with feeder protection functions.
S159: The Control Room Operator uses indications from the North Protection Panel to assess feeder protection operations and related alarms.
S160: The Transformer Protection Panel is dedicated to protection functions associated with the power transformer rather than feeder protection.
S161: The Transformer Protection Panel provides local indication of transformer protection operation for assessment during an alarm response.
S162: The Control Room Operator considers the condition of the Station DC System when alarms or protection indications suggest a possible control-power concern.
S163: A breaker status discrepancy is treated as an abnormal condition until its cause and operational significance are understood.
S164: The Engineering Workstation is used for authorized review of protection and event information, not as a substitute for immediate operational assessment.
S165: The Protection Relay Engineer supports investigation when relay indications, settings concerns, or event evidence require technical interpretation.
S166: The Substation Field Crew confirms device identity and local conditions before carrying out an authorized operation.
S167: The Substation Supervisor is consulted when the alarm response requires escalation beyond routine operator actions.
S168: The Control Room Operator produces the Clearance Handoff Memo when an unresolved alarm condition requires a formal handoff.
S169: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback before the associated state-change evidence is considered available for authorized engineering review.
S170: After handback, the Control Room Operator verifies that alarm status, equipment status, and recorded evidence are consistent before closing the response.
S171: The station communications design separates supervisory requests, bay-level execution, and protection action so loss of one layer does not silently substitute for another.
S172: Station Gateway brokers authorized station traffic across control-room and bay networks, applying configured protocol mappings, addressing, and access controls.
S173: It rejects malformed, stale, or unauthorized requests and records each rejection with enough context for operations review.
S174: Station Supervisory Control System presents available controls and indications to authorized operating personnel.
S175: Control Room Operator issues state-changing requests only through approved operating procedures and the configured supervisory interface.
S176: Bay Automation Controller validates each received request against local mode, interlocks, command authority, and equipment availability before issuing bay-level outputs.
S177: Breaker Control Unit applies accepted output commands at the breaker interface and returns the resulting position and circuit-health indications.
S178: Bay Automation Controller compares returned indications with the requested state and identifies incomplete or contradictory operation.
S179: Bay Automation Controller uses the inspection tag to associate the applicable equipment context with an authorized record.
S180: Station Gateway carries updated indications through the station interface using configured quality and timestamp attributes.
S181: Station Supervisory Control System displays indication quality and stale-data status so operators can distinguish a current value from a retained value.
S182: Sequence Event Archive retains time-tagged changes and control outcomes for event reconstruction and operational review.
S183: Satellite Time Receiver supplies the station time reference used to align event timestamps, subject to configured quality checks.
S184: Bay Automation Controller monitors communication health and places affected points in a defined degraded state when updates exceed configured age limits.
S185: Station Gateway reports link condition and protocol errors without converting a communication failure into an equipment-state change.
S186: Tandem evaluates electrical quantities against approved settings and issues protective trip outputs without relying on supervisory communications.
S187: North Protection Panel applies its assigned zone logic and maintains trip paths independently of supervisory network availability.
S188: Transformer Protection Panel applies its assigned protective logic and reports abnormal protection conditions through its configured interface.
S189: North Bay Controller maintains local bay control within the approved operating mode when supervisory communications are interrupted.
S190: South Bay Controller reports local mode and control availability through its configured bay interface.
S191: Engineering Workstation supports approved configuration review and does not serve as a routine source of operating commands.
S192: Maintenance Remote Terminal access is restricted to authorized maintenance sessions and is not used to bypass local interlocks.
S193: Station DC System supports control and protection functions through monitored station supply circuits, and supply loss is indicated as an abnormal station condition.
S194: Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection event records and verifies that approved settings remain consistent with coordination requirements.
S195: Substation Supervisor ensures communication changes, point mapping changes, and control logic changes are managed through station change control.
